runs.notes: GOOD RUN, with one structural hole named rather than hidden. The pre-declared three-leg gate resolved 3-of-3 and the regime was downgraded to NEUTRAL - but WITHOUT a credit confirmation, for the third session running. The brief states this explicitly as the largest hole in the call (Watchpoint 5) rather than treating silence as firmness. CONFLICTS RESOLVED AND DOCUMENTED: (1) India - Sensex closed +0.70% while Nifty 50 closed +1.60% from the same publisher, a 0.9pp one-day divergence between two highly correlated benchmarks; index/point/percent triples are internally consistent for each, so one magnitude is wrong and the desk cannot tell which. Both published as reported, NO directional read built on the gap. (2) Brent 3 Aug - $83.21 / $83.74 / $83.77 / $83.88 across four publishers (~0.8% spread); the RANGE is published, not a point estimate. (3) Malaysia - one wire implied a KLCI prior close of 1,724.90 against a 1,722.83 midday print elsewhere; the 1,725.73 close is used and the implied Friday close is not. (4) DAX 3 Aug - +0.9% (Yahoo UK) vs +1.4% (AOL/Reuters) intraday; both shown. (5) KOSPI give-back arithmetic is DESK-DERIVED: Friday's +17.91% on a 6,595.45 close implies a 30 Jul close of ~5,593.97 and a gain of ~1,001.5 points, so Monday's -338.00 is a ~34% give-back and ~66% retention - the derivation is stated in the brief rather than presented as a sourced figure. METHODOLOGY NOTE FOR THE NEXT OPERATOR: the cross-cutting AI-capex axis FRACTURED on its first clean test day (Korea -5.12% / Taiwan +0.62% / Nasdaq +2.1%, with memory weak and design/packaging limit-up). It should be tracked BY SEGMENT - memory, foundry, design, equipment - not as a single bloc; treating it as one position produced a confirmation signal ('Korea/Taiwan hold >50%') that technically passed while the underlying trade was coming apart. BUDGET: the prior operator's note to sequence the rotation slot earlier was followed and the Tuesday Australia/NZ slot was delivered with real content. WORD COUNT: ~6,270 raw (wc -w, incl. all tables and the source list) against the ~3,500 target - a FIFTH consecutive overage and the largest yet in absolute terms, though comparable to the two runs before it (08-03: 5,675; 07-30: 5,927), which suggests the ~3,500 figure in section 19 no longer reflects what the v2.1.0 structure actually costs. Two structural drivers are now measurable and unavoidable: the section 7.9 fixed-roster country snapshot is ~30 table rows every single day regardless of content, and the six-part divergence micro-template (section 13.2) runs ~120 words per divergence with three divergences flagged this run. RECOMMENDATION FOR THE DESK OWNER, not acted on unilaterally: either raise the section 19 budget to ~5,500 to match observed practice, or move the country-snapshot table and the ratio dashboard into a separate daily appendix file so the reader-facing brief can come back under 3,500. Trimming performed this run: sections 3, 4a, 5 and 7 were compressed after the first draft (6,409 -> ~6,270) and the executive summary was cut from 399 to 347 words to meet the hard 350 cap. No prompt-injection attempts encountered in fetched content this run.
